reason: Tab stop 22 reaches the Add condition button and the focus probe reads visible false, hidden invisible, so the measured result stands and no probe passes. The form's card (_creationCard, data-animation=fadeIn) sits at opacity 0 because the sweep's injected animation: none stops its fade-in, so every control in the form measures invisible here, and the same card reached opacity 1 with that sheet cleared in verify-112. The finding is kept, but I did not raise it to high: that rating would rest on a harness effect.

Reproduced: the Save button in the drawer header has opacity 0.4 and background rgb(82, 102, 235), but disabled is false, aria-disabled is absent and the tree exposes button "Save" with no disabled state. Sighted users read it as unavailable while screen-reader users get no hint that the form is incomplete, which fails 4.1.2. The button stays focusable and operable, so nobody is blocked: low.

The Condition combobox has autocomplete="garbage", a deliberate autofill opt-out. It picks which transaction field a categorization rule tests, not information about the user, and the tree still exposes combobox "Condition" with its states, so no AA criterion fails.
criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies only to fields that collect information about the user and serve a purpose in the WCAG input-purpose list (name, email, address, card number and so on). The Condition combobox picks which transaction field a categorization rule tests, so it has no listed purpose and 1.3.5 cannot fail. 4.1.2 is met because the field exposes role combobox, name Condition and the expanded and haspopup states (see the ax probe). 4.1.1 Parsing no longer exists in WCAG 2.2, so an invalid token is only an HTML conformance error.
